Jupiter governs growth, opportunity, and the confidence to reach for more than what already exists. Libra is the sign of balance, connection, and how we get along with each other. Together they make this a year where growth comes through who we meet and what becomes possible together: a friend's introduction leads to a creative collaboration, and the finished work reaches an audience neither person could have found alone. Jupiter spends about a year in each sign and takes about 12 years to visit all twelve.
rows.tension: Jupiter makes things bigger, and a few months in, the biggest thing is the list of what we have agreed to. Refusing feels rude, so we keep saying yes: another meeting, more of the work, another "it's fine" that is not true. Every extra request, correction, and follow-up starts going to the person who keeps saying yes. When a real choice comes up, we wait to hear what everyone else wants before saying what we want, and the decision goes to whoever speaks first. Somewhere along the way, being agreeable starts doing the work that honesty should be doing. The resentment stays quiet, because every one of these plans is something we technically agreed to.

rows.opening: When Mars enters Libra on {{entryDate}}, the song we have been shaping with a collaborator has several endings and no final version. Mars governs drive: how we act, assert ourselves, and fight for what matters. Libra is the sign of balance, connection, and how we get along with each other. One ending hits harder; another fits the rest of the song better, and we keep revising so neither preference is overruled. The care is useful: a choice made with attention to another response can become sharper than a solo decision. Mars usually spends roughly 6 to 7 weeks in each sign and takes about 2 years to move through all twelve signs. A retrograde can extend one sign stay to about 7 months.
rows.tension: Before the next rehearsal, we send another edit, ask for another reaction, and soften the strongest moment before anyone can object. Neither of us says which ending we actually want. No argument happens, but the song stays unfinished, and each of us starts resenting the other for a delay both of us are creating. The same social awareness that protects the partnership now keeps either side from taking a clear position.
rows.development: At the next rehearsal, we stop making new edits and play the existing endings aloud. We each say which version we prefer and why. One concern exposes a weak transition, so we fix it; the other is simply disappointment that a favorite version will not win. We choose the stronger ending, and the remaining rehearsal goes toward timing and delivery instead of reopening the decision.
rows.close: Before {{exitDate}}, we can leave one shared choice settled even if someone involved is still disappointed by it.

rows.opening: From {{entryDate}}, a community class that once handed out a page of notes starts sharing the same lesson as a voice note, a short video, and a searchable transcript. Uranus governs sudden change: breakthroughs, reversals, and the questioning of what we always believed. Gemini is the sign of curiosity, conversation, and options. A missed session no longer means losing the thread; someone asks a question in the daily message chain, another explanation appears, and the class starts teaching itself in several forms. This change has time to reshape habits rather than pass as a brief novelty. Uranus in Gemini takes about 84 years to move through all twelve signs and stays about 7 years in each sign.
rows.tension: The pressure builds when every new format promises to be quicker or clearer than the one already in use. The class moves from one thread to another, someone answers a difficult question with three more links, and an explanation gets abandoned when a fresher angle appears. The same willingness to experiment that made the lesson easier to access now scatters attention across unfinished versions. When a correction finally comes, the earlier wording is still being repeated, and the conversation changes subject before the mistake is settled.
rows.development: We do not need to defend the old handout or follow every new tool. We can keep the voice note that made the lesson easier to grasp, finish the explanation underneath it, and mark which claim changed after it was checked. If the message chain jumps to a new question, someone can return to the sentence left unanswered instead of adding another link no one has read. The chain gets quieter, and the corrected explanation is the one the class uses next time.
rows.close: Before {{exitDate}}, we can let one distracting format go.
try_this: We can finish one saved article or lesson before opening another tab on the same subject.
We can return to one message thread and answer the question we skipped when the subject changed.
We can compare one summary with its original source and correct one claim we repeated too quickly.

A conversation gets interesting enough to change the tone of a friendship. An unusual choice in clothes or art feels better than the version everyone already approves. We are drawn toward shared values, unfamiliar points of view, and relationships that allow separate lives.
rows.tension: The first difficult moment arrives when someone wants to know what the relationship is. We keep the tone casual after the heart is involved. We call a clear need a demand, or treat a reasonable expectation as proof that the bond has become conventional. Someone stops asking what the connection is because seeming unbothered feels safer than admitting it matters. Eventually, someone else takes that cool tone at face value and pulls back. The connection remains technically free, but no longer feels dependable.
rows.development: Friends may both feel the charge and keep treating it as a joke. Partners may assume time apart speaks for itself, even as one partner reads it as rejection. Nobody says anything because the arrangement is supposed to be easy. We can reject rules that never fit the relationship, but the absence of a rule is not an agreement. When nobody names what the relationship is, each person starts protecting independence from a demand that has not even been made.

rows.opening: After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Venus enters Pisces on {{entryDate}}, and attraction becomes softer, more imaginative, and harder to separate from hope. Venus governs relationships, creativity, and what we value. Pisces is the sign of imagination, compassion, and the edges that blur. A small kindness can feel deeply intimate. A song brings back a longing. We notice beauty in what is unfinished, and affection moves through gestures that ask for no credit.
rows.tension: That openness also makes missing information easy to decorate. We explain away mixed signals, spend past our limit to make something lovely, or help before anyone has asked. Each act feels generous on its own. Together, they can build an arrangement around what we hope is there rather than what is being returned. We keep stepping in before anyone asks, so their pain stays at the center while our disappointment gets renamed as patience.
rows.development: During this transit, affection can stay attached to possibility after the facts have changed. We cover the cost again, accept a vague answer, or keep making exceptions because each choice seems small. The total is not small. Generosity stops creating closeness and starts protecting an ideal from evidence. Art and tenderness can deepen a mutual relationship. In a one-sided exchange, the same gestures can keep the imbalance looking meaningful. What has someone actually offered? What have we supplied because the imagined version felt too beautiful to lose?
rows.close: By {{exitDate}}, sympathy and hope can leave us doing all the work for a relationship that only felt mutual.
try_this: We can ask what kind of help is wanted before stepping in to solve anything.
We can set a cash limit before buying a gift or covering someone else's expense.
We can play one album while drawing, cooking, or arranging a shelf only for pleasure.

rows.opening: Chiron returns to Aries on {{entryDate}} after moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, bringing the pressure back to wanting, beginning, and taking up space. Chiron carries the wound that teaches: hurt, healing, and the deeper work of integration. Aries is the sign of courage, beginnings, and going first. A hand rises, then drops. A clear preference becomes "either is fine." In another moment, the freeze is covered by an answer sharper than the question.
rows.tension: Chiron in Aries exposes the tender spot around wanting, beginning, and existing without apology. Acting before confidence arrives can interrupt the old response that made silence feel safer. But when every hesitation feels shameful, movement becomes a test of worth. We force an answer, treat a pause as rejection, or push past a limit just to prove nobody can stop us. What began as courage leaves no space for uncertainty, and the original fear still decides the pace.
rows.development: Chiron last moved through Aries from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}, and this return puts the same pressure back into ordinary moments. Someone volunteers to go first, then spends the rest of the day replaying how it looked. At a family table, a sibling stops laughing along with the old joke about being too much. Elsewhere, a simple no holds through the silence that follows. The wound around identity remains. What changes is how we carry it. A want is spoken without becoming a demand. A refusal stands without turning into a fight.
rows.close: Before {{exitDate}}, a swallowed want leaves the decision to someone else.
try_this: We can go first in one low-stakes moment where we usually wait for a cue.
We can ask for one wrong order to be corrected in a calm sentence.
We can repeat one clear no in the same tone when someone pushes again.

rows.opening: The North Node in Aquarius and the South Node in Leo move attention from the name on the work to what a group can make together. After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, the North Node enters Aquarius and the South Node enters Leo on {{entryDate}}, and shared purpose starts carrying more weight than personal recognition. The Nodes point the growth story: the North Node asks for the unfamiliar direction, the South Node asks for release. A group keeps the best idea even when it came from the least visible contributor. A creative part still matters after the group changes it.
rows.tension: The South Node in Leo knows how to catch attention and give an idea a memorable face. That skill can make shared work easier to notice. The cost appears when every project also has to confirm who is special. We pull a group effort toward the contributor with the biggest audience, defend our part after a better version appears, or lose interest when credit spreads around. The North Node in Aquarius keeps pointing to the shared result, while the need for applause keeps asking for center stage.
rows.development: The Nodes last occupied the Aquarius-Leo axis from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. An idea becomes more useful when its originator lets someone else improve it. A group gets further when credit reflects actual contributions instead of settling on the familiar name. The unfamiliar part is staying invested as attention spreads out. Another voice may become the public face, and the first spark no longer owns the outcome. Creative expression remains real without applause. If we keep demanding proof that our part mattered, the group spends its energy protecting status instead of developing the idea.
rows.close: Before {{exitDate}}, shared projects lose useful ideas whenever every change has to preserve one name at the center.
try_this: We can bring one idea to a shared project and accept one change that makes it more useful, even if the final version looks less like ours.
We can name the contributor whose work improved a group result, especially when someone else is getting the attention.
